answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01, a party statement published by NVIDIA about its own new compute business model; it also relays quotes and plans from partner AI clouds Sharon AI and Firmus.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says a new model lets AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers through a revenue-sharing and credit-support arrangement. Under it, AI clouds sell NVIDIA-powered cloud services, and NVIDIA earns both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity.
findings.use: Supports the limited conclusion that NVIDIA has publicly announced a commercial model in which it earns product revenue plus a share of partner cloud revenue, backed by credit support, for AI-cloud capacity built on its platforms.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is the party that designed and announced the model, so it can state the model's structure, but it is a company statement and not an independent report or a contract. The announcement does not give the revenue share percentage, the amount of credit support, the counterparties, or any signed volumes, so it establishes the announced structure only.
findings.next_check: Look for NVIDIA's 10-Q or 10-K disclosure of these arrangements, including how revenue sharing and credit support are recognized, their size, and any guarantee or receivable exposure, plus named partner agreements.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says the model gives it a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream and accelerates adoption of its platforms among high-growth AI-native customers.
findings.use: Lead for a possible shift in NVIDIA's revenue mix toward usage-linked, recurring income, to be tested against disclosed revenue lines before it is treated as a valuation input.
findings.grounds: The claim is NVIDIA's own characterization of the economics and is forward-looking. It rests on partner cloud revenue, which NVIDIA does not report in this article, and the article gives no share, timing, or volume figures. The main uncertainty is how large the usage-linked stream would be relative to product sales and whether it persists after the AI-cloud partners' capacity is in use.
findings.next_check: Check whether NVIDIA reports any line item or disclosure for revenue from revenue-sharing arrangements and whether that line grows across the next two annual filings, and compare it with product revenue.

findings.claim: NVIDIA describes credit support as part of the model that makes AI-cloud procurement of its infrastructure possible for capital-constrained emerging AI companies, which the article says have had limited access to capital even with long-term commitments.
findings.use: Lead for a possible financial risk: NVIDIA may take on credit or counterparty exposure to AI-cloud partners and their end customers, which could affect receivables, guarantees, or losses if those partners cannot pay.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is best placed to describe its own model, but the article does not state the form, amount, duration, or triggers of the credit support, and it does not say whether NVIDIA would be liable. The risk is an analyst inference from the words credit-support model. The source supplies only the premise that the customers are capital-constrained.
findings.next_check: Search NVIDIA's filings for guarantees, residual value commitments, financing arrangements, or off-balance-sheet obligations tied to AI clouds, and for any increase in receivables or related-party exposure.

findings.claim: Firmus is building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, which it expects to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
findings.use: Conditional lead for a large potential NVIDIA GPU deployment through an AI-cloud partner. It supports a scenario in which this campus becomes a meaningful source of NVIDIA system demand if the build-out proceeds on schedule.
findings.grounds: The figures are a partner's expected scale, relayed by NVIDIA in its own announcement, so they are a plan and not a confirmed build or an order. Firmus is the direct party to the plan, while NVIDIA's role is as supplier under the same model. The main uncertainty is whether the campus is built, the timing, the GPU mix, and whether NVIDIA supplies all of the GPUs or only a part.
findings.next_check: Look for Firmus or NVIDIA disclosure of construction milestones, power contracts, a financing close, and GPU purchase or delivery terms for the Batam campus, and for any NVIDIA statement of how much of the 170,000 GPUs it expects to supply.

findings.claim: Sharon AI's CEO says the company is collaborating with NVIDIA to deliver sovereign, large-scale AI compute infrastructure.
findings.use: Supports the narrower conclusion that Sharon AI, as a named partner, describes a collaboration with NVIDIA on sovereign AI compute. It does not show scale, economic terms, or deployment.
findings.grounds: The speaker is Sharon AI's cofounder and CEO and is in a position to describe the partnership, but the quote is promotional and was relayed in NVIDIA's announcement. It confirms a relationship, not its volume or the timing of any NVIDIA supply.
findings.next_check: Look for Sharon AI's own filings or announcements with the GPU count, facility location, capacity timing, and whether the collaboration includes NVIDIA credit support or revenue sharing.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says AI-cloud companies are already building DSX AI factories to serve customers and workloads across regions.
findings.use: Lead that the model is in early execution across several partners and regions. It does not establish how many factories exist, their capacity, or how much NVIDIA revenue they produce.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is the speaker and knows its own program, but the statement is general and undated as to completion, with no count of factories, locations, or capacity. It can be read as a sign of adoption rather than measured deployment.
findings.next_check: Check NVIDIA's later announcements or partner disclosures for a list of DSX AI factories with locations, capacity, and online dates, and whether NVIDIA reports them in its results.

findings.claim: The article names AI natives Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI as examples of where compute demand is going, saying they need immediate access to AI-cloud capacity for training, post-training, fine-tuning and agentic inference.
findings.use: Lead for the demand segment NVIDIA is targeting. It does not show that these companies buy from the model, use NVIDIA-powered capacity, or pay NVIDIA through this arrangement.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA names these companies as illustrations of demand, not as parties to the arrangement. The article gives no contracts, volumes, or statements from them, so the link to NVIDIA revenue is not established. Only a stated general need is supplied.
findings.next_check: Check whether Baseten, Fireworks AI or Together AI disclose any use of NVIDIA-powered AI-cloud capacity or any agreement that names NVIDIA or a partner cloud as a provider.
